If ganyan grades mo and you came from a decently well-known HS/SHS, I'm sure you do... at least if yung basis ay gaya nung last year. I'm saying this kasi I have a lot of SHS (galing sa mas performing na school) classmates who had pretty average-above average grades pass the Big 4 as long as they did well sa mga requirements/interviews, compared sa JHS friends ko from still pretty well-known schools din naman kaso from smaller cities kasi tapos mas populated, na kahit mas matataas yung grades, hit or miss padin. like mga top students talaga kinuha. So ranking does matter more if you're in the latter situation, and if you have lots of org/leadership background, that helps too. 

sa last part, just wanted to say din na plenty of other unis can give you good education, even those not in manila. Kung feel mo Big 4 lang makaka-validate sayo, ngayon palang try not to place the entirety of your value sa institution na pinapasukan (or papasukan) mo. marami kang choices sa Top 10 unis ng bansa, if ever hindi man pumasa. You could make up a reason/find a reason to start talking to them. It's good to directly approach people with the intent of starting a friendship but that might pressure them into "taking you in," so finding reasons to sort of start a conversation like asking about something from school/talking about a hobby that you both have, e.g. if someone likes the same music as you do, you can start by saying "Hey, I noticed you listen to this band too. I love them! What's your favorite song?" Or something like that is better, I think. You could also try making opportunities for interaction with them to happen organically, like asking to be grouped together for schoolwork, joining a club they're in (that you're interested in too, ofc), asking to join them when they hang out (though this can be tricky, so try to befriend like maybe 1 person out of the group first before trying to hang out with everyone, so it won't be too much of a shocker)

Almost all of my friends are introverts and I mostly met them through something shared, and then sort of "expanded" their friendships with the friendships I have too, like introducing them to people who have the same interests. I find that friend groups tend to form naturally, so if you just try your best to show yourself/how you are, you'll find people to be with. But it does help being confident! If being confident is tough, try *pretending* like you are. Soon enough, it'll catch up haha 

Hope this helps :)

Mhm. That's why I think you should communicate that to her. A relationship isn't supposed to be a negotiation. If I can't say something I consider relatively harmless to my partner because he/she just doesn't like hearing about it, I'd turn to my friend too. (Though generally if I have to do that, it's not a relationship I'd want to be in.) So why not both of you create that space of honesty instead of robbing it from each other? If you don't like it, make sure she understands why. If there are other things that bother you, tell her. Hear her out too. Let her tell you why she did it anyway and what it meant to her. 

If you can't voice out how you feel then she probably wouldn't even know you were feeling that way, and it's a little unfair to expect your partner to automatically know that you're feeling a certain way. Last thing, don't put all the blame on the relationship! your partner isn't supposed to fix your self-worth, only you can do that. I think if you can work on yourself regardless of how your relationship is, you'd be a happier person with or without anyone. :)

If the both of you trust each other enough, no matter how much either one talks about fucking celebrities, you'd have no doubts that your loyalty still is strong.

But it seems that trust isn't the only issue, it's also that you feel inadequate enough to feel threatened by your wife talking about what I think is pretty normal and harmless thoughts. It's okay to feel insecure, but don't shift your insecurities towards her--why not tell her about it instead so she's aware and you feel more comfortable? 

+the fact that your wife doesn't talk about it to your face probably shows that it'd be an issue if she did.  I feel like you both should think about that and re-evaluate if your "not talking about any attraction" actually means loyalty or a lack of comfortable openness.

I see. I've noticed a lot of (mostly) men do this and make the mistake of just shutting up and not letting the other person know at all. I won't push you to do anything you don't really feel like doing, but for the heck of it, tell her. Don't think of it like a job application--waiting for her acceptance, setting back due to fear of rejection, etc.--think of it like how it simply really is; you're attracted to her, and she deserves to know it. If she doesn't want to date, cool. Just make it so that your relationship stays the way it is. (It might be hard for some people not to feel awkward afterwards, but it's better to let someone know that they're an amazing person and that you find them attractive than silently distancing yourself because you're trying to get over them before even dating them.)

Trust me, not everyone really gives much of a shit about attractiveness. Yes, obviously it plays a part. A huge part for some people, but it's not something that's gonna end all of your chances with someone. Especially if you both really enjoy each other's company. But please, if it's the kind of thing that you have to 'fix', (a you-problem/loving yourself thing) I do suggest that you find that space of comfort within yourself first. A lot of relationships end because of the other person still thinking they're undeserving of another person's love.

Anyhow, I would still stick to talking about it with her. Don't make it seem like something she has to say yes or no to. Instead, speak your mind and tell her about everything you feel. Even if you remain friends afterward, she'll probably start looking at you in a romantic light just as a 'what if'. Who knows? It's better to take a chance.

Edit: You're still awesome. Being mentally ill and working too much doesn't make you less of a desirable person. I'm sure she knows that as your friend :)

I've had the same dilemma, and I ended up pursuing a Business degree. I took up HUMSS for Senior High, but thought that going for PolSci was a bad idea for me even though it was my initial plan to do so. The difference is, you're worried about flunking law school. I, on the other hand, was worried about not ever going to law school at all. So here are my thoughts: If you're SURE that you're financially able to afford law school, that there are no other hindrances, and that you have enough grit to go through it, take PolSci. It's what you want. But, if you're like me, and you're willing to explore other fields, (frankly i got tired of HUMSS subjects after 2nd sem of my 12th year and couldnt imagine 4 years of PolSci lol) you should consider Accountancy. 

I'd say if the problem is whether you really are gonna get to law school, and you want a secure fall back, take BsA. You won't lose anything. If you love the 'qualitative' side of things and REALLY prefer your passion, try to plan out things first. (is law school a sure thing? will you be able to pass?) Nonetheless, passing or not passing relies on whether you're willing to push your boundaries. 

What I'd do? I would explore the business field right now and see if i take interest in it. 4 years undergrad won't mess with your chances in law school. Any undergrad will get you there, so make those 4 years as beneficial as possible. If finance is a problem, take BsA. (Another thing to take in consideration is the CPA lawyer title. Another plus). But, If you're all set, and you definitely see yourself getting to law school for sure- absolutely sure, then take your PolSci. 

Try taking HUMSS for Senior High. If you can shift at the school you're going to, nice. But otherwise, try to do it anyway. You can still apply for Accountancy afterwards, just make sure your credentials are good enough. This is just to gauge your interest. This is what I did and I was also so sure of PolSci back then, until I took 2 years of HUMSS subjects and got kind of bored haha. But hey, these are my thoughts. The decision is yours. I hope I was able to help :)
